notes: The github/docs repository README says its documentation and content folders are CC BY 4.0 and its code MIT, and its LICENSE file holds the CC BY 4.0 text, which doesn't license trademark rights (GitHub's name and logos). That is the licence of the repository's content files. docs.github.com itself couldn't be reached, but the same repository holds the site policy it publishes, and on 2026-11-18 its Terms of Service and Acceptable Use Policies were read there. They don't mention the documentation's licence, and they cut both ways: the Terms reserve only rights "not expressly granted to you under this Agreement or by law", while the Acceptable Use Policies forbid reproducing or exploiting "any portion of the Service" without written permission and list research and archiving as the uses of information from the Service, however it was obtained. GitHub is both the licensor of the docs and the author of those terms, so whether they narrow the README's CC BY grant for a paid app is for the owner to decide; until then it stays link only. (The other catalogue sources read from GitHub repositories are licensed by their own authors, not by GitHub, so these terms aren't their licensor's.) Only content files in the repository are CC BY; the repository's site-building code is separate. Product documentation: the Get Started section is general Git, the rest is specific to GitHub.
